verdict.line: You lose if you trade face-to-face before level 3 and let Tahm stack 3 An Acquired Taste for a free Devour; you win if you wait for your full W/E/Q kit and wall him in for an isolated burst.

brief.thesis: Tahm's only kill tool is Devour (R), which needs 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste built through champion-damaging autos or Q (Tongue Lash) hits — stacks Yorick can simply deny by not feeding him free trades before level 3. Once Yorick has W (Dark Procession) and E (Mourning Mist) online, he can block Tahm's exit with the wall and shred/slow/mark him with E for a lopsided trade. That's the structural reason the 56.8% win rate over 111 games skews Yorick's way despite the matchup starting even.

theirWindow.what: He can Devour you for magic damage and follow with W (Abyssal Dive) to land on an area near terrain, knocking you up and isolating you from help. Back off and reset instead of trading face-to-face once he's at 2-3 stacks.

yourWindow.when: W and E both off cooldown
yourWindow.what: Drop W (Dark Procession) to wall off his retreat, then hit E (Mourning Mist) for the armor shred, slow and mark, and close with Q's (Last Rites) empowered auto. Every champion hit by Q digs a grave, so this trade also feeds your Mist Walkers.

start.why: 47.3% win rate over 55 games as the lead start; the sustain and damage reduction on hit absorb Tahm's Q pokes and auto trades before you have your full kit at level 3.

boots.why: 64.8% win rate over 54 games; Tahm's passive, Q, and Devour all hit for magic damage, so the magic resist directly blunts his all-in burst.

core.why: 70% win rate as the opener in the top core path; the stat spike is your biggest single power jump and lines up with your level 9-11 trading window.
Follows Trinity Force in the 70% win-rate path; the armor shred stacks with E's (Mourning Mist) own armor reduction for a bigger burst window once you've walled him in.
Closes out the 70% win-rate, 11.2%-pick core path; ability haste shortens your Q (Last Rites) cooldown for more grave digs per trade.

runes.keystoneWhy: 60% win rate over the largest sample (32.3% pick); the sustain and permanent health growth let you win the war of attrition against a champion whose own passive scales off total health.

summoners.why: 60.2% win rate and the highest pick rate (60.8%) in this matchup; Teleport supports your split-push identity with Maiden and Mist Walkers, while Flash lets you disengage before he can land Devour or the Abyssal Dive follow-up.

playing.title: Farm safe before level 3
playing.detail: Before you have one point in Q, W, and E, avoid extended trades — Tahm's Q (Tongue Lash) pokes you for free at 900 range, slows you, heals him on a champion hit, and builds his Acquired Taste stacks.

playing.title: Wall then mark once level 3 hits
playing.detail: With your full basic kit up, drop W (Dark Procession) to block his exit, hit E (Mourning Mist) for the armor shred, damage, slow and mark, then finish with Q's (Last Rites) empowered auto.

playing.title: Track his stack count all lane
playing.detail: Watch for 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste — that's the moment Devour (R) becomes a live threat and he can swallow you for magic damage before following up.

playing.title: Respect Abyssal Dive near terrain
playing.detail: W (Abyssal Dive, 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown) damages and knocks up an area on landing; don't stand near walls or ledges he can dive onto after stacking Devour.

playing.title: Bank graves off every champion hit
playing.detail: Q (Last Rites) always digs a grave on a champion hit regardless of the trade's outcome; stack 3+ graves before committing to an extended skirmish so your Mist Walkers can swarm him.

playing.title: Force fights once Trinity Force completes
playing.detail: Trinity Force is your clearest power spike in the build path; look to initiate trades around level 9-11 once it's online rather than waiting for him to all-in first.

brief.patchCaveat: All items, runes, summoner spells, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning (wall-and-mark trading, grave timing, stack tracking) is my own tactical read, not sampled data.

stats.opponentTip: Tahm Kench will get a kill if he manages to close in, so try to engage combat only after reaching level 3. Pull lane and farm before reaching level 3. Trap him inside [W] and hit him with [E] to gain the upper hand.
